segments.line: Monday. Mo
bets you can't skate down Dead Man's Hill.
Nobody has ever made it to the bottom. You
don't make it either. You hit the curb at full speed,
fly over a parked van and land face first in a hedge. You
stand up. You pick a leaf out of your hair. Mo
drops his phone. "
Do it again."
Tuesday, you try code number four. Money. A soft chime, and a
sports bag drops onto your bed.
Inside, twenty-five stacks of hundred-dollar bills. Two hundred and fifty thousand dollars. You
enter it again. Another bag. By dinner, you've stopped counting bags and started counting rooms. You buy
pizza for the whole school. Eleven hundred pizzas. The delivery driver cries a little. It has been
raining for three days, so you try code number two.
Sunshine. The clouds just slide apart over your town, and only your town. On
TV, the weather lady stops mid-sentence and stares at her map.
Wednesday. Code number seven. A low
rumble, a flash, and a red sports car drops out of thin air onto your driveway.
Brand new. Keys in. You're
fourteen. You can't drive. You make another one anyway. In blue.
Ellie wants a pony. There's no pony code. She settles for a car.
Thursday. Code number nine. Jetpack. It arrives with a
bang, strapped to your back, and you go straight up so fast your shoes stay on the lawn. You
fly to school above the traffic jam, over the bus, where everyone presses their faces to the windows, over the
principal's car, and
land on the school roof just as the bell rings. Mo is
waiting. He's been waiting since seven. "
Okay. Okay. Jetpack. Me next."
For four days, you're the luckiest person who has ever lived.
Then, on Friday morning, you smell something burning. And you look down.
